title: Marketing web3: Audience, Community, More

reader_summary.headline: This is Steph, and welcome back to the A6C podcast.
reader_summary.overview: This is Steph, and welcome back to the A6C podcast. We have a bunch of exciting episodes in the hopper from hardware to healthcare to fintech, and more. But today we're coming to you with a feed drop from our sister podcast, Web3 with A6C.

key_points.text: Now, this episode is all about marketing, and it relates to the common startup fallacy, if you build it, they will come.
key_points.evidence_quote: Now, this episode is all about marketing, and it relates to the common startup fallacy, if you build it, they will come.

key_points.text: And with the exception of outliers, many of us have learned the hard way that, in fact, without distribution, they won't come.
key_points.evidence_quote: And with the exception of outliers, many of us have learned the hard way that, in fact, without distribution, they won't come.

key_points.text: But equally important, as the tools to build become more accessible than ever, your ability to capture attention also matters more than ever.
key_points.evidence_quote: But equally important, as the tools to build become more accessible than ever, your ability to capture attention also matters more than ever.

key_points.text: In this episode, longtime host Sonal Choxi sits down with A6C Crypto CMO Kim Milosevic and also Amanda Cassat.
key_points.evidence_quote: In this episode, longtime host Sonal Choxi sits down with A6C Crypto CMO Kim Milosevic and also Amanda Cassat, who helped bring Ethereum to market.

thesis: The episode argues that the common startup fallacy that 'if you build it, they will come' is incorrect because distribution is essential for success. It further posits that marketing is a matching exercise between a product and the people who would use it if they knew about it, rather than simply putting unwanted items in a user's field of attention.
